title: Day 84 · Week 12, Day 0 — Body: the reflex kit — the startle, the grasp, the suck and the swallow, the gut that comes home from the cord, the fifty-six percent sex call, and the three feeding cues you'll read at four in the morning
summary: Week 12 opens, the last full week of the first trimester. Your baby is about 5.4 cm head to bottom (NHS), skeleton hardening, placenta likely feeding them. The Body episode is the reflexes: what a reflex is and why a baby with almost no cortex can run one (spinal and brainstem circuits; MedlinePlus); the startle, seen from ~8 weeks and one of the movements that rises then falls (de Vries, Visser & Prechtl), becoming the newborn Moro reflex with its brainstem centre and diagnostic weight (Futagi 2012); the palmar and plantar grasp and the AAP timetable for when each newborn reflex fades; sucking and swallowing, the fetus as a heavy drinker for its size (Ross & Nijland 1997) and why no ultrasound can measure how much; the gut returning from the umbilical cord (still visible in 5% at 12 weeks; Bogers 2019); why a first-trimester sex call is at best 56% right (Bogers 2018); and why suck–swallow–breathe coordination is one of the last skills to mature (Lau 2016), with the three AAP feeding cues — rooting, sucking, hand to mouth.
action: Open the pregnancy file and add a section called 'First weeks' with two lines: 'Feeding cues: rooting, sucking, hand to mouth. Feed before the crying.' and 'Reflexes fade: stepping and startle by about two to four months, rooting by four, palm grip by six, fencing by seven, foot grip by twelve.'
